College of Engineering and Computer Science
Become a Leader in Industrial and Systems Engineering
If you want to acquire the advanced knowledge needed to become a creative researcher, technical leader, and technology innovator in industrial and systems engineering, our PhD program at the University of Michigan-Dearborn is for you.
The degree is a full-time, research-based program designed to equip you with the cutting-edge knowledge, technical skills, and abilities to conduct original, high-quality translational research in industrial and systems engineering.
To lessen financial concerns, all PhD students receive full funding in the form of appointments as a graduate student instructor, a research assistant, or both. The appointments provide a monthly stipend, health insurance, and a tuition waiver. Students are guaranteed full funding for up to five years provided they maintain good academic standing and adequate progress toward their degree.
Where a PhD in Industrial and Systems Engineering Will Take You
Earning the PhD places you on the fast track to a prosperous career in various industries requiring profound technical knowledge, research ability, and leadership skills. You could be a pioneer for change in a high-tech corporation, lead a team in advancing healthcare systems, or even become a university professor, spreading knowledge to the next generation of engineers.

Industrial Engineers
Employment of industrial engineers is projected to grow 12 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations.
About 23,100 openings for industrial engineers are projected each year, on average, over the decade. Many of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, such as to retire.
